title: Conditional mutual information bounded by left entropy
statement:
Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be measurable random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, taking values in countable spaces and each attaining only finitely many values. Then the conditional mutual information of $X$ and $Y$ given $Z$ is bounded above by the Shannon entropy of $X$:
\[
  I[X : Y \mid Z ; \mu] \;\le\; H[X ; \mu].
\]
(The bound also holds trivially when $\mu$ is the zero measure.)
hypotheses_covered: values in countable spaces (discrete, with measurable singletons)
each of X, Y, Z has finite range
replaced:
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $Z$ under a zero-or-probability measure with finite ranges,
\[
  I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;\le\; H[X;\mu].
\]
